title: Does Centralized Learning Help Embodied Agents Coordinate, and When Can a Tabular Study Tell?
abstract: arXiv:2601.17454v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Tabular studies are a common way to compare independent and centralized multi-agent learners, because they avoid function approximation. A natural expectation is that centralized learning, which learns joint actions, helps agents coordinate, especially when their bodies make solo success hard. Earlier work tests this only in parts: it measures coordination for one learning method, compares methods with the agents' bodies fixed, or varies speed but reports only how well the team did. We test it in a predator-prey environment, where teammates cooperatively hunt together while two teams compete. We compare independent Q-learning (IQL) with central Q-learning (CQL) in all four predator and prey pairings, under limits on speed and stamina, on a 5x5 and an 8x8 grid trained for 200,000 episodes each, and check that the agents learn on both. We measure coordination directly, with predictions for the main measurement fixed in advance. I

translated_title: 集中式学习是否有助于具身智能体协调，以及表格化研究何时能够回答这一问题？
translated_abstract: 表格化研究是比较独立式与集中式多智能体学习器的常用方法，因为它避免了函数逼近。一个自然的预期是，学习联合动作的集中式学习能够帮助智能体实现协调，尤其是当其身体条件使单独成功变得困难时。以往的工作只部分地检验了这一点：或者仅针对一种学习方法度量协调性，或者在与智能体身体固定的情况下比较不同方法，或者改变速度但只报告团队的整体表现。我们在一个捕食者-猎物环境中对此进行测试，其中队友之间合作捕猎，而两个团队相互竞争。我们在所有四种捕食者与猎物的配对中，在速度和耐力受限的条件下，比较独立Q学习（IQL）与中心化Q学习（CQL），在5x5和8x8网格上各训练200,000个回合，并验证智能体在两种情况下均能学到策略。我们直接度量协调性，并对主要测量指标预先确定了预测。
tldr: 该论文在捕食者-猎物环境中，于多种捕食者与猎物配对及不同网格规模下，系统比较独立Q学习与中心化Q学习，并通过预先设定的直接协调性度量来检验集中式学习何时真正有助于具身智能体的协调。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically compares independent Q-learning with centralized Q-learning across predator-prey pairings and grid sizes, directly measuring coordination with pre-specified predictions to determine when centralized learning actually helps embodied agents coordinate.
